verdict: TSMC's revenue rose 39% to NT$868.5B ($26.9B) on strong demand for its industry-leading 3- and 5-nanometer technologies — and with a 59.0% gross margin, it kept NT$374.7B ($11.6B) as profit, up 57% in a year.

segments.name: High-performance computing
segments.note: Chips for AI data centers and servers — 53% of everything TSMC sells, and up 19% from the third quarter.

segments.name: Smartphone
segments.note: Chips for phones — 35% of revenue, up 17% from the third quarter.

segments.name: Internet of Things
segments.note: Chips for connected devices of every kind.

segments.name: Digital consumer electronics
segments.note: Chips for TVs, game consoles and gadgets.

segments.name: Others
segments.note: Everything else, including older-node specialty work.

opex.name: Operating expenses
opex.note: Research, engineering and running the business side of the fabs — shown as one line, including other operating expenses, net.

otherDetail: Non-operating income of NT$23.1B (about $0.7B) — mostly interest income earned on TSMC's cash pile, plus foreign-exchange gains and a share of profits from associates, partly offset by finance costs and other losses.
footerNote: TSMC reports in New Taiwan dollars (revenue NT$868.5B; net income attributable to shareholders NT$374.7B). Dollar figures are converted at NT$32.31 per US$1 — implied by TSMC's own stated US-dollar revenue of $26.88B. Operating expenses are shown as one line, as in TSMC's earnings release, combining operating expenses with other operating expenses, net, and segment dollars are the platform shares from TSMC's official Q4 2024 materials applied to revenue. The tax line is set so the flow lands on net income attributable to TSMC shareholders.
follow100Note: For every $100 TSMC took in, $43.14 survived as profit. AI data-center chips (high-performance computing) supplied $53.00 of the $100 — and advanced nodes (7-nanometer and below) made up 74% of wafer revenue.

takeaways.title: AI chips run the show
takeaways.text: High-performance computing — mostly AI accelerators — was 53% of revenue and rose 19% from the third quarter; smartphone chips were another 35%, up 17% on seasonal launches.

takeaways.title: Margins jumped in a year
takeaways.text: Gross margin reached 59.0%, up from 53.0% a year ago, and net margin was 43.1% — TSMC charges premium prices for leading-edge capacity nobody else can supply, so profit grew 57% on 39% revenue growth.

takeaways.title: A huge building budget
takeaways.text: TSMC set its 2025 capital budget at $38–42B and guided Q1 2025 revenue of $25.0–25.8B with a gross margin of 57–59% — a seasonal step down, with AI demand still growing underneath.
